criteria.reasoning: Identifies several ethical issues (public safety, professional integrity, reputation, QA timeframe) with significance, links to engineering design and organisational pressure of six-month cycle, and lists all relevant stakeholders with impact.

criteria.name: Balanced Discussion — Discusses objective arguments for and against decisions of the ethical issues. Draws a conclusion on how stakeholders should make decisions about the issues.
criteria.reasoning: Provides objective for and against arguments with appropriate depth (competitive advantage, revenue, job security vs harm, trust, legal costs) and trade-offs, drawing a clear Not Ship conclusion. Lacks explicit decision-making recommendations differentiated for several stakeholders.

overall: Well-structured ethics report with balanced pros/cons, strong stakeholder awareness, and appropriate use of case studies and EA Code. Meets all task requirements with justified Not Ship recommendation. Weakness is absence of visuals, quantitative evidence, and limited stakeholder-specific recommendations.

feedback.summary: You produced a well-structured, balanced report with a justified Not Ship recommendation. Your introduction and stakeholder analysis are excellent, and your argument structure is compelling. To improve, you need stakeholder-specific decision guidance, quantitative evidence, and required visual elements.
next_steps: For C2 Excellent: in DISCUSSION and The Most Ethical Path, add explicit recommendations for Rachel, her company, the chip contractor, and the health department, not just Rachel.
For C4 Excellent: add quantitative evidence for costs, failure rates or recall impacts alongside your Engineers Australia, HSSIB and Volkswagen case studies.
For C5 Very Good/Excellent: add at least two visual elements, e.g., stakeholder impact matrix and risk trade-off table, cited in-text.

criteria.C1: You excelled here. In INTRODUCTION you identified public safety, integrity, reputation and QA pressure, linked to competitive design pressure, and listed all stakeholders including end-users. Keep this depth for future tasks.
criteria.C2: You built objective for/against arguments with trade-offs in DISCUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship. For Excellent, you need recommendations for several stakeholders, not just a single Not Ship conclusion for Rachel.
criteria.C3: Your logic from pros to cons to The Most Ethical Path is compelling and your CONCLUSION is well-supported. You showed systematic understanding of harm severity to end-users and company-wide integrity.
criteria.C4: You substantiated well with Engineers Australia Code, HSSIB/BBC and CNBC sources. To reach Excellent, add quantitative data such as failure probability, cost of recall, or NHS impact stats alongside qualitative cases.
criteria.C5: Your ABSTRACT, INTRODUCTION, body and CONCLUSION are fluent with consistent referencing. To move to Good or higher, you must include visual elements (figures/tables) correctly labeled and referenced in text, as rubric requires.
